initial.title: [CI][runners] Make larger-runner eligibility branch-independent and observable
initial.goal: Make larger-runner eligibility branch-independent while retaining repository scope and providing fast native diagnostics for capacity versus policy failures.
initial.required_outcome: A typed read-only Rust preflight proves runner label and capacity, group visibility, selected repository access, workflow restriction state, and stale workflow references, while PR branches remain eligible without allowlist mutation.
authority_boundary: GitHub organization runner and runner-group settings remain external authority.
The preflight is read-only and reports observed state without mutating it.
Repository scoping remains mandatory while workflow restriction must be disabled for branch-independent eligibility.
operator_constraints: Never write tracked issue changes on main.
Use Rust and existing COTS crates; do not add shell or Python control-plane logic.
initial.task_boundary: Fix issue #32 only: branch-independent larger-runner eligibility diagnostics and focused CI integration proof.
deliverables: Typed csdlc-github runner-preflight request and result contracts, including bounded live job observation.
Read-only Octocrab inspection of hosted runner, runner group, repository access, workflow restrictions, and stale refs.
Focused unit and loopback integration tests.
Live preflight and PR canary evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Normal PR branches can acquire the configured larger runner without branch allowlist changes.
Runner group access remains explicitly limited to agent-logic/agent-design-language.
Preflight reports label, group visibility, repository access, workflow restriction state, and stale workflow refs without secrets.
Diagnostic classification distinguishes capacity unavailable, policy ineligible, and configuration-eligible but non-dispatching jobs.
A live PR canary assigns a runner and reaches a terminal result.
non_goals: Mutating organization settings from the preflight
initial.plan_summary: Build a small read-only Rust preflight on existing COTS GitHub surfaces, wire a fast workflow gate, prove policy/capacity classification, review exact head, and publish a live canary PR.

steps.action: Define the typed runner policy and capacity contract.
Implement Octocrab-backed runner and group inspection with stale-ref diagnostics.
Add focused deterministic tests and CI contract routing.
Review exact head, publish, and retain the live runner-assignment canary.

risks: GitHub API response shape may drift
Token permissions may make state indeterminate
A Ready runner may have transient capacity delay
stop_conditions: The fix would require broadening repository access or using AWS
initial.review_scope: Typed request/result schema, GitHub endpoint selection, policy/capacity classifier, stale-ref handling, redaction, and focused tests.
review_prompts: Can policy-ineligible or non-dispatching routing still be misreported as capacity unavailable?
Does eligible require explicit target-repository selection and workflow restriction off?
Can any credential or authorization header appear in output?
Are stale workflow refs reported without becoming false eligibility authority?
initial.failure_policy: Fail closed with typed indeterminate or ineligible diagnostics; never infer eligibility from runner Ready alone.

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove typed classification, parsing, redaction, and loopback GitHub API behavior.
Prove the preflight remains a focused branch-independent gate in the canonical workflow.
Reject malformed tracked changes before review.
Prove group 3 is repository-scoped, workflow-unrestricted, the hosted label is visible, and the PR job receives a runner and terminates.
validation_lanes.defer_reason: Requires live organization settings and the published issue #32 PR head.
